column2: What object type does text I/O expose, and how does it handle a byte-based backing store?
column3: It exposes str objects and transparently encodes or decodes bytes, with optional newline translation.

column2: How can an API forwarding encoding=None make its callers receive EncodingWarning when they omit an encoding?
column3: It can use text_encoding(); the documentation recommends considering UTF-8 defaults for new APIs.

column2: What happens if IOBase.close is called twice, and what happens to later reads?
column3: Closing an already closed stream has no effect; subsequent operations such as reading raise ValueError.

column2: Will IOBase.writelines insert line endings between the supplied strings?
column3: No; the supplied lines normally need to include their own separators.

column2: How does RawIOBase.readinto distinguish end of file from temporarily unavailable nonblocking input?
column3: For a nonempty buffer, zero means EOF; None means no bytes currently available in nonblocking mode.

column2: Does FileIO guarantee complete writes and reads of the requested size?
column3: No; writes and reads may be short. Buffered binary I/O provides write-all and read-at-least behavior.

column2: What does TextIOBase.read return when size is negative or None?
column3: A single string containing characters read through EOF.

column2: Why can text I/O be slower than binary I/O, and why are text tell and seek costly?
column3: Character-codec conversions add overhead; tell and seek also require a reconstruction algorithm.

column2: How do JSON and pickle differ in whether their serialization format is textual or binary?
column3: JSON is a Unicode text format, often encoded as UTF-8; pickle is binary.

column2: Which pickle protocol became the default in Python 3.8, and what improvements did it introduce?
column3: Protocol 4; support for very large objects, more object kinds, and data-format optimizations.

column2: Must callers specify a protocol when using pickle.loads, and are trailing bytes consumed as another object?
column3: The protocol is detected automatically; bytes after the object's representation are ignored.

column2: How can pickling dispatch be customized for one Pickler without replacing the global table?
column3: Assign a dict-like dispatch_table to the instance; a subclass-level table can instead supply the default for that subclass.

column2: Does pickling a class preserve the class's code and class attributes?
column3: No; classes are recorded by fully qualified name, rather than serializing their code or data.

column2: If a class defines both __reduce__ and __reduce_ex__, which does pickle prefer and what extra argument does it receive?
column3: It prefers __reduce_ex__, which receives the integer protocol version.

column2: What must the sender provide to keep PickleBuffer data out of the main pickle stream?
column3: A buffer_callback to the Pickler or dump/dumps; collected buffers are represented by cheap markers instead of copied data.

column2: Which Unpickler method can be customized to restrict loading global classes and functions?
column3: Unpickler.find_class, called whenever a global class or function is requested.

column2: How can object members be listed without invoking descriptors, __getattr__, or __getattribute__?
column3: Use inspect.getmembers_static, which returns name-sorted pairs and accepts an optional predicate.

column2: Where does inspect.getdoc look when a class or method has no documentation string of its own?
column3: It looks through the inheritance hierarchy; an invalid or missing result yields None.

column2: What ordering and uniqueness constraints does inspect.Signature validate in its parameters argument?
column3: Names must be unique, positional-only parameters precede positional-or-keyword ones, and defaulted parameters follow nondefaulted ones.

column2: What information does inspect.getargvalues return for a frame?
column3: An ArgInfo tuple containing argument names, the varargs and keyword-argument names or None, and the frame's locals dictionary.

column2: How does inspect.get_annotations process string values when eval_str is true?
column3: It evaluates string values using eval to undo stringized annotations.

column2: Why can retaining references to interpreter frame objects delay destruction and increase memory consumption?
column3: The references can create cycles that keep reachable objects alive longer, so cycles should be explicitly broken.

column2: In what order are frames returned by inspect.stack?
column3: The caller's frame is first and the outermost frame is last.

column2: What capability does the CO_ITERABLE_COROUTINE flag give a generator?
column3: It makes it a generator-based coroutine usable in await expressions and able to yield from coroutine objects.

column2: If loop.stop is invoked during run_forever, when do callbacks newly scheduled by the current callbacks run?
column3: The current batch completes, but newly scheduled callbacks wait until the next run_forever or run_until_complete call.

column2: Which context does loop.call_later use when no context argument is supplied?
column3: The current context is used; callers may instead provide a custom contextvars.Context.

column2: What must a custom event-loop task factory accept and return, and how is the default restored?
column3: It accepts loop, coro and all keyword arguments, forwards those keywords and returns a Task-compatible object; setting the factory to None restores the default.

column2: When loop.create_connection receives an existing connected socket, may host and port also be supplied?
column3: No; host, port, family, proto, flags, happy_eyeballs_delay, interleave and local_addr must not be specified with sock.

column2: What are family, proto and flags used for in loop.create_datagram_endpoint?
column3: They are integer socket-module constants passed to getaddrinfo for host resolution.

column2: What happens when loop.create_server gets port=0 or None and the host resolves to multiple interfaces?
column3: An unused random port is selected, potentially a different one for each interface.

column2: Does asyncio's subprocess API directly decode output streams into text?
column3: No; the returned bytes can be converted to text with bytes.decode.

column2: What does Server.wait_closed wait for starting with Python 3.12?
column3: Both server closure and completion of all active connections.

column2: What does zipfile.is_zipfile use to recognize a ZIP archive, and can it accept a file-like object?
column3: It checks the magic number and accepts a filename or file-like object.

column2: Which compression methods ignore ZipFile's compresslevel, and what ranges apply to DEFLATED and BZIP2?
column3: STORED and LZMA ignore it; DEFLATED accepts 0 through 9 and BZIP2 accepts 1 through 9.

column2: If ZIP header metadata flags conflict with metadata_encoding, which encoding instruction wins?
column3: The archive header flag takes precedence over the Python-specific metadata_encoding setting.

column2: Can other archive members be read or written while a writable ZipFile.open handle remains open?
column3: No; attempting it raises ValueError.

column2: What happens if ZipFile.read encounters an unsupported compression method?
column3: It raises NotImplementedError; a missing corresponding compression module also causes an error.

column2: How does ZipFile.write handle a null byte in the chosen archive member name?
column3: The archive member name is truncated at the null byte.

column2: Does zipfile.Path sanitize member filenames to prevent path traversal?
column3: No; the caller must validate or sanitize them, for example using resolved paths and commonpath.

column2: What name does ZipInfo.from_file use when arcname is omitted?
column3: The original filename with its drive letter and leading path separators removed.

column2: At what position should a file object passed to tarfile.open initially be?
column3: Position zero.

column2: If an exception occurs inside a writing TarFile context manager, is the archive finalized?
column3: No; only the internally used file object is closed.

column2: How does TarFile's dereference option change the treatment of symbolic and hard links?
column3: False stores links; True stores their targets' contents, with no effect on systems without symbolic links.

column2: Why does TarFile.extractall apply directory metadata after extracting the members?
column3: Creating files resets directory modification times, and restrictive directory permissions could otherwise prevent extraction.

column2: How does TarFile.errorlevel=2 differ from the default level 1 during extraction?
column3: Level 1 raises fatal errors; level 2 also raises nonfatal errors as TarError exceptions.

column2: What base path is used for symbolic-link versus hard-link targets in TarInfo.linkname?
column3: Symbolic targets are relative to the containing directory; hard-link targets are relative to the archive root.

column2: What happens when a tar archive contains several versions of the same file?
column3: Later versions are expected to overwrite earlier ones, which enables updates but can be abused.

column2: What file-size and linkname limits does the POSIX ustar format impose?
column3: An 8 GiB maximum file size and linknames up to 100 characters.
